concept.name: News trading
concept.definition: A short-horizon style that trades the price impact of scheduled announcements (earnings, central-bank decisions, economic data) and unscheduled events, entering just before or immediately after the release to capture the volatility burst. Most news traders operate intraday, since the exploitable reaction is typically short-lived.
concept.intuition: News is the one scheduled source of volatility: everyone knows when the payrolls print lands, nobody knows its content - the game is positioning for, reacting to, or fading the crowd's reaction better than the crowd.
concept.mechanics: Prepare scenarios and alerts around the economic calendar; trade the initial directional reaction, the buy-the-rumor-sell-the-news unwind, or the fade once enthusiasm peaks. Stops must accommodate post-release volatility, and spread widening and slippage around releases are structural costs.
concept.failure_modes: Spreads widen and liquidity vanishes exactly at the release, so theoretical fills are unavailable, and algorithmic reaction times leave discretionary traders structurally late; fading a genuinely regime-changing headline is a standing source of large losses.
concept.misconceptions: That knowing the news content is the edge; prices react to the surprise relative to expectations, not the headline itself - a good number can sell the asset off if it was not good enough.
concept.example: A trader shorts EUR/USD strength minutes after a payrolls beat that fell short of the whisper number, covering an hour later as the initial dollar spike fades.
